A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a rapid, eikaryotic, in-vitro selection method using antibody-ribosomes-mRNA (ARM)-complexes as selection particles.

ARM selection provides the following advantages: (a) the selection particle is a complex of antibody and ribosome, which is a more efficient particle than a single antibody for selection of high-affinity binders; (b) the selection particle carries the genetic information as ribosome-bound mRNA, which makes possible single-step PCR amplification; and (c) the ribosome-bound RNA is protected against RNase digestion and is therefore stable during selection and PCR amplification.

we have developed an eukaryotic in vitro method for antibody display and evolution that uses ARM complexes as selection particles and that is based on single-step RT- PCR for amplification of genetic information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ARM complexes can be used as selection particles for in vivo and in vitro display and selection of antibody and non-antibody binding sites.
the ribosome is an efficient and versatile selection particle for in vitro display of proteins and peptides.
the ARM complexes can be used to select and evolve antibodies, receptors or peptides from large libraries in a rapid, eubacterial or eukaryotic in vitro system.
